items.title: George Guesnon Interview
items.q: But one thing he did tell me... We were talking about chords one night, you see.

ctx.x: Here's something I want you to... Even if I have to interrupt your train of thought. There was one nice little thing you told me about once when you worked with Albert Glenny. He told you that pick out a good man to watch and then ask him questions and things like that. Do you remember? What was that he said to you once? Something about... Well, yeah, well... What was some advice he gave you?

Well, the older men had all kind of things. I mean, I don't so well remember that answer. But one thing he did tell me... We were talking about chords one night, you see. And he says, this is one thing about music. He said, D minor might be the right chord. It might be the right chord. He says, but if everybody in the band would make A7, we'll say. But they make it together, then it's the right chord. He says, but where it becomes a bad chord is if two is making D minor and the other fellow is making A7. Then you…

There's another thing I remember you've talked about, which we never did get on tape, that you're not ashamed to ask people questions to show you something. Whereas some musicians will try to act like they know it all already, and they're ashamed, you know, to ask somebody to show them anything. But you say, in the old days, you'd get together and you'd watch somebody and show me how to do that.
